newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends slightly up in calm after storm.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends slightly up in calm after storm.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart in scant trade on Wednesday, with the market taking a breather after its recent stormy sessions, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.771 against Tuesday's T$27.778 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a light US$207.5 million.
The Taiwan dollar, beset by strong foreign funds outflow triggered by a big stock market correction, fell on Monday to an 11-month low of T$27.759 and extended its decline on Tuesday.
"Investors could not decide whether the Taiwan dollar has room for further decline, so many just stepped to the sidelines instead and watched," said one dealer.
She said the rate likely would hover at current levels for a short time before the Taiwan dollar resumes a slow descent.
A T$27.75-79 range was seen for Thursday.
